key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage concentrated near the buried hole-transport-layer interface in p-i-n perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive screening can guide buried-interface design, with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification reducing UV damage and improving film and device stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL, and ideality-factor measurements.
Compare UV-soaked films and devices with different ITO modifiers.
evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements localized preferential degradation at the HTL interface, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, and showed reduced damage with interface modification.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or evidence that the approach generalizes beyond the tested UV-soaking conditions and device stacks.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
